clue.text: Hereafter, God somehow could be met

indicators.note: done somehow, in some unspecified way, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: the letters taken as written
the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A pious musing that in the afterlife, by God's grace, people might meet again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' links the wordplay to the definition at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To foregather is to assemble or gather together, so the past tense is a formal synonym for met.

clue.text: Like office job associated with the vicar?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: relating to clerks and office paperwork
second meaning: relating to the clergy

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses come from the same root: clerks were originally clerics, the literate people of the church.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective covers both desk work done by clerks and anything to do with clergymen such as a vicar.

clue.text: Sword carried by the peer

indicators.note: the answer is carried inside the words that follow, spanning them

parts.note: the hiding words, read straight through across the space

explanation.surface: A nobleman wears a sword at his side.
explanation.definitionFit: An épée is the fencing weapon with a stiff triangular blade, one kind of sword.

clue.text: Design military event?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a picture inked into the skin
second meaning: an evening display of military music and marching

explanation.walkthrough: The Edinburgh Military Tattoo is the best-known example of the military show.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a permanent skin decoration and a drum-and-bugle display put on by soldiers.

clue.text: Man perhaps getting under vehicle left in city

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece placed under another is written after it

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
the Isle of Man is an example of an island

explanation.surface: A mechanic slides under a car parked somewhere in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person under the car, but it is the Isle of Man, signalled by 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Carlisle is a cathedral city in Cumbria, in the far north-west of England near the Scottish border.

clue.text: Something hairy: like this answer!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: fine soft hair or feathers, as on a chick or a peach
second meaning: this answer runs ... the grid

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition refers to the clue's own place in the grid: it is a Down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means fluffy fine hair and is also the direction of this entry in the grid.

clue.text: Servicemen take bits off part of ship

parts.note: OR, other ranks, the soldiers who are not officers
to lop is to cut off branches or parts

explanation.surface: Soldiers are dismantling a section of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The orlop is the lowest deck of a sailing ship, so it is one part of the vessel.

clue.text: Not how to run a business? One's perplexed

definitions.text: Not how to run a business

definitions.meaning: second meaning: someone baffled is said to be ...

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful literal reading of the idiom as running a loss-making company.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at a loss is an idiom for being bewildered and unsure what to do or say.

clue.text: He stops a gent — mad rush

indicators.note: the letters are driven mad, thrown into a crazy new order

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone halts a man who is in a frantic hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Stepping on the gas is an idiom from pressing a car's accelerator, meaning to hurry up.

clue.text: Most weird street by English lake

parts.note: Lake Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A road beside a lake in England that is the spookiest of all.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means strange and frightening, so the superlative is a synonym for weirdest.

clue.text: Weapon knight protected in fine material

indicators.note: the knight is shielded by being placed inside the material

parts.note: lace is a delicate openwork fabric
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A knight's weapon is wrapped in delicate cloth for safe keeping.
explanation.walkthrough: N for knight comes from chess notation, since K is taken by the king.
explanation.definitionFit: A lance is the long spear carried by a mounted knight when jousting.

clue.text: People up a sort of tree

definitions.meaning: the surface suggests climbers perched in branches
the setter means a family tree, where forebears sit at the top

explanation.walkthrough: The picture is of people stuck up in a real tree; the tree is a genealogical chart.
explanation.definitionFit: Forebears appear higher up a family tree than their descendants, so these are earlier generations of a family.

clue.text: Riches'll upset German author

indicators.note: upset as in knocked over, so the letters tumble into a new order

parts.note: the letters taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Wealth will unsettle a German writer.
explanation.walkthrough: The contraction 'Riches'll' is an odd phrase chosen purely for its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Schiller was the German poet and dramatist who wrote the Ode to Joy and William Tell.

clue.text: Slushy stuff, mostly fine

indicators.note: most of the word but not all of it, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: good, as in 'that's fine'

explanation.surface: A sticky mess that is largely acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Goo is a sticky or sentimental substance, matching both senses of something slushy.

clue.text: In gambling the Parisian appears bright

indicators.note: the French article is placed in the gambling word

parts.note: gaming is betting on games of chance
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: A Frenchman at the casino looks sparkling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appears' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Gleaming means shining brightly, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Henry, stop wasting time!

parts.note: to halt is to stop

explanation.surface: An order to someone called Henry to quit dawdling.

clue.text: House with new steamer for food some won't eat?

indicators.note: the letters are made new, put into a fresh order

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A house with a new steam cooker turning out something not everyone will touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse flesh is eaten in parts of Europe but many people, especially in Britain, refuse it.

clue.text: Report soldiers behind schedule

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
late means not on time

explanation.surface: An account that some troops are running late.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate a story is to tell or narrate it, so it is a synonym for report.

clue.text: Magnificent drink knocked back

parts.note: lager is a light beer

explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' is slang for drinking quickly, which is the surface sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Regal means kingly, fit for royalty, so splendid or magnificent.

clue.text: Information about lake in valley

indicators.note: the information word goes about, around, the lake letter

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

clue.text: Story about a sheep in Wyoming city

indicators.note: the story is placed about, around, the other pieces

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story
taken as written
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.definitionFit: Laramie is a city in south-eastern Wyoming, home of the state's university.

clue.text: Anger — last thing needed by older generation

parts.note: the word whose final letter is taken
an age is a generation or era

clue.text: Most profound river, something proving to be a nuisance

clue.text: Army officer briefly getting round a port

parts.note: Gen is the short form of General
O is round in shape
taken as written
